angle: Where other training materials jump to update equations, this video stays entirely with the idea that learning means rolling downhill on a squared-error cost surface, building from one-input slopes to the 13,000-dimensional gradient-as-importance picture without computing a single weight gradient.
angle_detail: Watch [02:31]-[05:09] first for how the cost averages squared output errors over tens of thousands of MNIST examples, then [05:51]-[11:37] for slope-proportional steps, local minima and gradient components as per-weight importance. Pitfall: a local minimum need not be the global one, and the hidden patterns end up looking random rather than edge-like. Backprop itself is deferred, so pair this with the series' backprop video for any computation.
